log.text: Light Screen up on P2's side
Light Screen ended on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega Gengar-Mega. Lead Gengar+Sneasler: mega turn1 Shadow Tag trap, Sneasler Fake Out stops Whimsicott Tailwind/Grimmsnarl screens, Rock Slide 4x vs Charizard-Y. Back Sinistcha Heatproof walls sun Heat Wave, Rage Powder protects Gengar, Staraptor Intimidate + Tailwind + Brave Bird vs Whimsicott/Quaquaval.
decisions.notebook: Opponent relies on Charizard-Y Drought + Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind and Grimmsnarl screens. Sneasler 189 Speed outspeeds max Zard 167 and Whimsicott 168. Sinistcha Heatproof is key fire wall. Keep Fake Out for Prankster stops.

decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard-Mega-Y+Whimsicott to establish sun+Tailwind immediately. HeatWave spread in sun pressures both opponents, aiming to KO Gengar before Shadow Tag locks us in. Whimsicott Prankster Encore can lock opponents into bad moves. Back two Archaludon+Grimmsnarl provide defensive typing, screens, and pivoting to handle Kingambit and Dragonite threats.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent has Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag), Sneasler (FocusSash, Unburden, fast FakeOut), Sinistcha (RagePowder, Heatproof), Dragonite (Multiscale, LumBerry, Tailwind), Kingambit (LifeOrb, SupremeOverlord, SuckerPunch), Staraptor (Intimidate, SharpBeak). My Mega is Charizard-Y (Drought). Plan: Lead Charizard+Whimsicott for sun+Tailwind, KO Gengar turn 1 with HeatWave spread. Back Archaludon+Grimmsnarl for screens, Steel/Dragon pressure, PartingShot pivoting. Watch for opponent leading Gengar+Sneasler or Dragonite+Staraptor for double Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler 189 outspeeds and Fake Out has +3 priority, stopping Prankster Tailwind. Gengar 178 then OHKOs Whimsicott with Sludge Bomb (176-460%). Mega traps Charizard with Shadow Tag, preventing switch after losing support.
decisions.notebook: Opp core is Zard-Y Drought + Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind + Grimmsnarl screens. Sneasler 189 > max Zard 167 and Whimsicott 168. Sinistcha Heatproof walls sun. Plan: deny Tailwind with Fake Out, KO Whimsicott with Sludge Bomb/Poison Jab, trap Zard with Mega Gengar Shadow Tag.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler FakeOut (+3) outspeeds Prankster Tailwind (+1), but can only flinch one mon. Choosing Heat Wave + Mega for Charizard ensures Drought activates even if flinched. Whimsicott Tailwind gives speed control if it acts. Heat Wave spread pressures both foes, aiming to KO or heavily damage Gengar before it can trap with Shadow Tag.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent leads Gengar+Sneasler. Gengar has Gengarite (Shadow Tag Mega), Sneasler has Focus Sash + Unburden + FakeOut. My Mega is Charizard-Y (Drought). Plan: Lead Charizard+Whimsicott for sun+Tailwind, KO Gengar turn 1 with HeatWave spread. Back Archaludon+Grimmsnarl for screens, Steel/Dragon pressure, PartingShot pivoting. Watch for opponent leading Gengar+Sneasler or Dragonite+Staraptor for double Tailwind. Opponent tendencies: aggressive leads with fast FakeOut + Shadow Tag setup.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl's Prankster Fake Out flinches Sneasler, preventing a lethal Rock Slide on Charizard. Charizard's Heat Wave then KO's the weakened Sneasler and pressures Gengar-Mega into Protect. Grimmsnarl also resists Gengar's Ghost and Fighting moves, making it the ideal switch-in to maintain momentum and set up screens next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent leads Gengar+Sneasler. Gengar has Gengarite (Shadow Tag), Sneasler has Focus Sash + Unburden. My Mega is Charizard-Y. Plan: KO Gengar with Heat Wave spread. Back Archaludon+Grimmsnarl for screens and pivoting. Opponent tendencies: aggressive leads with fast FakeOut + Shadow Tag. Grimmsnarl Fake Out works on Sneasler but fails on Ghost-type Gengar. Archaludon Thunderbolt KO's Gengar but leaves Charizard exposed to Sneasler's Rock Slide.

decisions.rationale: Both ours 14-16% die to Heat Wave. Sneasler loses to +3 Fake Out before Rock Slide. Gengar immune to Fake Out and has Protect. Switching Sneasler to Sinistcha makes Fake Out fail (Ghost immune) and Heatproof halves Heat Wave, preserving Gengar with Protect and keeping Sneasler sash intact for later.
decisions.notebook: Opp is sun hyper offense: Mega Zard Y Drought Heat Wave/Weather Ball/Hurricane/Protect Timid, Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast/Protect Bold Leftovers, Grimmsnarl Prankster Fake Out/Reflect/Light Screen/Parting Shot Light Clay Impish. Likes Tailwind + screens. Our plan: deny Tailwind with Fake Out + Sludge Bomb, trap Zard with Mega Gengar Shadow Tag, wall sun with Sinistcha Heatproof immune Fake Out, use Staraptor Intimidate for physical pivots Archaludon/Quaquaval/Stunfisk.

decisions.rationale: Weather Ball (Fire in sun, 100 power, 100% accuracy) guarantees KO on 16% Gengar-Mega. Grimmsnarl Fake Out flinches Sneasler, preventing its dangerous Rock Slide (4x vs Charizard). Even if Gengar Protects, Sneasler is neutralized at 14% HP. This minimizes risk compared to 90% accuracy Heat Wave which could miss and leave Charizard exposed to Rock Slide.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega (Gengarite/Shadow Tag) + Sneasler (Focus Sash/Unburden). Sneasler Fake Out only works first turn out; Unburden doubles speed after Focus Sash consumed. Charizard-Mega-Y 4x weak to Sneasler Rock Slide. Grimmsnarl 2x weak to Gengar Sludge Bomb and Sneasler Poison Jab. Weather Ball becomes Fire type in sun with 100 power and 100% accuracy. Plan: KO Gengar with Weather Ball, flinch Sneasler with Fake Out, then bring Archaludon for screens and cleanup. Opponent tendencies: aggressive leads with fast Fake Out + Shadow Tag pressure. Archaludon Thunderbolt KO's Gengar but leaves Charizard exposed to Sneasler Rock Slide if not flinched.

decisions.rationale: Gengar at 16% dies to any Charizard spread anyway; Rage Powder does not redirect Heat Wave. Best is to ensure Grimmsnarl dies before screens: Sludge Bomb 89-214% + Matcha Gotcha chip guarantees KO, Sinistcha Heatproof + healing lets it survive sun Heat Wave. Sac Gengar after value.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO: Mega Zard Y Drought Heat Wave/Weather Ball/Hurricane/Protect Timid, Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast/Protect Bold Leftovers, Grimmsnarl Prankster Fake Out/Reflect/LightScreen/Parting Shot Light Clay Impish. Likes Tailwind + screens. Our counter: Fake Out + Sludge Bomb to deny Tailwind, Mega Gengar Shadow Tag to trap Zard, Sinistcha Heatproof walls sun and immune Fake Out, Staraptor Intimidate for physical pivots.

decisions.rationale: Zard is 95% under sun with Light Screen up. Rock Slide is 4x physical bypassing screen and best KO chance vs Zard. Sneasler at 14% still has Focus Sash to survive Heat Wave and proc Unburden for speed control next turn, while Staraptor Brave Bird is only neutral and risks OHKO.
decisions.notebook: Opp is sun HO Mega Zard Y + Prankster Whimsicott Tailwind + Prankster Grimmsnarl screens. Likes Light Screen + sun boosted Heat Wave/Weather Ball. Our plan: Fake Out deny Tailwind, Mega Gengar Shadow Tag trap Zard, Sinistcha Heatproof walls fire, Staraptor Intimidate + Tailwind for physical pivots Quaquaval/Archaludon/Stunfisk-G.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Charizard-Mega-Y)
decisions.rationale: Weather Ball in sun is 100% acc Fire 100bp, dealing 67-196% to Gengar-Mega at 16%—guaranteed KO removing Shadow Tag. Light Screen cushions Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha (15-47% → ~12-35%) and Shadow Ball. Even if Gengar Protects (reduced rate), screen is up and Gengar remains at 16% for next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega (Gengarite/Shadow Tag) + Sneasler (Focus Sash/Unburden). Sneasler Fake Out only works first turn out; Unburden doubles speed after Focus Sash consumed. Charizard-Mega-Y 4x weak to Sneasler Rock Slide. Grimmsnarl 2x weak to Gengar Sludge Bomb and Sneasler Poison Jab. Weather Ball becomes Fire type in sun with 100 power and 100% accuracy. Plan: KO Gengar with Weather Ball, flinch Sneasler with Fake Out, then bring Archaludon for screens and cleanup. Opponent tendencies: aggressive leads with fast Fake Out + Shadow Tag pressure. Archaludon Thunderbolt KO's Gengar but leaves Charizard exposed to Sneasler Rock Slide if not flinched. Turn 3 plan: Weather Ball Gengar + Light Screen to remove Shadow Tag and protect vs Sinistcha special attacks. After Gengar KO'd, switch Grimmsnarl to Archaludon for cleanup with Thunderbolt/Flash Cannon/Draco Meteor. Sinistcha weak to Fire (Weather Ball/Hurricane/Heat Wave) and Dark (Parting Shot doesn't damage). Archaludon resists Grass and Ghost, good vs Sinistcha. Kingambit/Dragonite/Staraptor still unrevealed—expect one as next switch. Kingambit Sucker Punch priority +1 threatens Charizard; Dragonite ExtremeSpeed priority +1 also threatens. Staraptor Intimidate + Brave Bird/Close Combat high damage. Keep Grimmsnarl healthy for screens vs physical threats.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sneasler 14% dies to any spread unless redirected. Rage Powder forces both foes into Sinistcha which resists with Heatproof + Light Screen (Heat Wave ~21-54% after both). This lets Sneasler free Rock Slide 60-180% spread 4x vs Mega Zard Y for possible OHKO and chip Archaludon. Preserves sash if intact.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO with Mega Zard Y Heat Wave/Weather Ball, Prankster Whimsicott Tailwind, Prankster Grimmsnarl Light Screen/Reflect. Leads with Zard+Whim. Uses Light Screen early. Our counter is Heatproof Sinistcha + Mega Gengar Shadow Tag trap + Fake Out deny. Staraptor Intimidate/Tailwind still unused for late game vs Quaquaval/Stunfisk.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler at 14% HP is guaranteed KO'd by Flash Cannon. Protect shields Charizard from 4x Rock Slide while Archaludon tanks the spread hit at 0.5x. Leaves favorable Charizard+Archaludon vs Sinistcha matchup with Fire super effective.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega+Sneasler. Sneasler Focus Sash consumed, Unburden active (137-189 speed). Charizard-Mega-Y 4x weak to Rock Slide. Archaludon resists Rock (0.5x), Flash Cannon KOs low-HP Sneasler. Sinistcha Heatproof, weak to Fire (Weather Ball/Hurricane/Heat Wave 2x). Kingambit/Dragonite/Staraptor unrevealed. Plan: KO Sneasler, then use Charizard's Fire moves vs Sinistcha. Keep Archaludon healthy for Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon cleanup vs physical threats. Light Screen active 7 turns protects vs special attacks.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler 189 outspeeds Zard 115-167 and Arch 90-137, Rock Slide 4x Zard 65-160% spread + Shadow Ball 21-46% secures KO through Light Screen reduction. Sun ends this turn, removing Zard threat. Sneasler at 14% will faint anyway, then Staraptor Intimidate/Tailwind cleans Quaquaval/Stunfisk late.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO Mega Zard Y Heat Wave/Weather Ball/Hurricane/Protect Timid, Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Encore, Grimmsnarl Prankster Light Screen/Reflect/Fake Out Light Clay, Archaludon Modest Stamina Wise Glasses Thunderbolt/Flash Cannon/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand, Quaquaval Jolly MysticWater. Leads Zard+Whim, sets Light Screen early. Our Heatproof Sinistcha walls Fire, Mega Gengar Shadow Tag trap, Sneasler Fake Out + Unburden sash. Plan Staraptor Tailwind late vs Quaquaval.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Sneasler's raw Speed range (137-189) overlaps Charizard's 167; if outsped, Rock Slide 4x KOs Charizard at 95%. Protect guarantees safety while Archaludon's Draco Meteor (130 BP, neutral) heavily damages Sinistcha toward a KO next turn. Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha is 0.25x on both targets, so no urgent pressure. Preserving Charizard for Fire coverage vs Sinistcha and cleanup is priority.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Gengar-Mega fainted turn 3 to Weather Ball. Whimsicott/Grimmsnarl fainted early. Sneasler Focus Sash consumed, Unburden active (137-189 Spe), 14% HP. Sinistcha Heatproof, 60% HP, weak to Fire (Weather Ball/Heat Wave/Hurricane 2x). Archaludon Def +1, 93% HP. Light Screen 6 turns. Sunny Day 1 turn left. Opponent has Dragonite (Lum, Multiscale, Jolly), Kingambit (LO, SupremeOverlord, Adamant), Staraptor (SharpBeak, Intimidate, Jolly) unrevealed. Plan: KO Sinistcha with Charizard Fire moves next turn, then clean with Archaludon Draco/Flash Cannon. Keep Charizard alive for sun-boosted Weather Ball vs remaining threats.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon at 88% with +2 Def -2 SpA -1 Atk. Double Fighting is only super-effective physical we have. Sneasler 14% will die anyway, so trade it for max damage. Staraptor CC adds second hit; even with Stamina +3 after first hit, combined range can KO. Light Screen irrelevant to physical. Protecting Staraptor leaves Archaludon alive.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO: Mega Zard Y Timid Heat Wave/Weather Ball/Hurricane/Protect, Whimsicott Bold Prankster Tailwind/Encore, Grimmsnarl Impish Light Clay Reflect/Light Screen/Fake Out/Parting Shot, Archaludon Modest Stamina WiseGlasses Thunderbolt/Flash Cannon/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand EQ/Ice Fang/TWave/Protect, Quaquaval Jolly MysticWater AquaStep/CC/IceSpinner/Protect. Tends lead Zard+Whim, sets screens early. Our plan: Heatproof Sinistcha walls Fire, Mega Gengar Shadow Tag, Sneasler Fake Out sash Unburden, Staraptor Intimidate Tailwind late.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt Sneasler has ~93% KO chance at 14% HP despite SpA -2. Sneasler outspeeds but Fake Out is only 0.5x. Removing Sneasler simplifies to Staraptor 1v1 where Archaludon's Def +2 and Light Screen help survive physical hits. Draco/Flash Cannon are weaker with SpA -2.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Archaludon SpA -2 from Draco Meteor, Def +2 from Stamina. Sneasler Unburden active (137-189 Spe), Focus Sash consumed. Staraptor Intimidate activated, Sharp Beak. Light Screen 5 turns remaining. Opponent back: Dragonite (Lum, Multiscale, Jolly, 93-145 Spe), Kingambit (LO, Supreme Overlord, Adamant, 55-102 Spe). Plan: KO Sneasler with Thunderbolt, then use Archaludon's Def +2 to handle Staraptor. Watch for Dragonite Extreme Speed priority or Kingambit Sucker Punch if Archaludon is weakened.

decisions.rationale: Staraptor last mon vs Archaludon 16% +4 Def -2 SpA. CC is only move with SE 2x vs Steel/Dragon; Brave Bird is 0.5x. Even with +4 Def, 16% is in KO range for CC, while Thunderbolt still threatens OHKO. Must attempt KO now; Protect loses tempo 1v2.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO: Mega Zard Y Timid Heat Wave/Weather Ball/Hurricane/Protect, Whimsicott Bold Prankster Tailwind/Encore, Grimmsnarl Impish Light Clay screens, Archaludon Modest Stamina WiseGlasses TBolt/Flash/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand EQ/Ice Fang/TWave/Protect, Quaquaval Jolly MysticWater AquaStep/CC/IceSpinner/Protect. Leads Zard+Whim, sets screens early. Future: preserve Intimidate, need Tailwind late vs Quaquaval.

decisions.rationale: Staraptor moves first and KOs into 16% with either STAB-boosted Brave Bird or super-effective Close Combat. Protect blocks both, preserving Archaludon's massive Def +4. Thunderbolt only wins if foe misplays with Tailwind/Protect; opponent's clear line is Close Combat to finish. Protect extends the game and keeps options open.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Archaludon SpA -2 (Draco), Def +4 (Stamina x3 + Intimidate). Staraptor Def -1, SpD -1, Sharp Beak, Jolly. Light Screen 4 turns. Foe back: Dragonite (Lum, Multiscale, Jolly, 93-145 Spe), Kingambit (LO, Supreme Overlord 3 allies, Adamant, 55-102 Spe). Plan: Protect now. If Staraptor Tailwinds, Thunderbolt next. If Staraptor keeps attacking, Protect until PP out or switch. If Archaludon KOs Staraptor, expect Dragonite ExtremeSpeed or Kingambit Sucker Punch priority; Archaludon too weak to survive either.

decisions.rationale: Staraptor faster but +4 Def Archaludon lives any physical hit (CC 43-92% vs 0 Def, ~14-30% at +4) then Thunderbolt 143-230% OHKO. Only Protect avoids immediate loss and forces opp action/switch with Light Screen ticking.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO: Mega Zard Y Timid Heat Wave/Weather Ball/Hurricane/Protect, Whimsicott Bold Prankster Tailwind/Encore, Grimmsnarl Impish Light Clay screens, Archaludon Modest Stamina WiseGlasses TBolt/Flash/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand EQ/Ice Fang/TWave/Protect, Quaquaval Jolly MysticWater AquaStep/CC/IceSpinner/Protect. Leads Zard+Whim. Preserve Intimidate, need Tailwind late vs Quaquaval.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Staraptor outspeeds (115-167 vs 105) and both Close Combat and Brave Bird guaranteed KO Archaludon at 16% HP. Thunderbolt only wins if Staraptor doesn't attack, but even then Archaludon at 16% SpA-2 can't survive Dragonite/Kingambit. Protect gives 50% chance to survive and extends the game.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Archaludon SpA -2, Def +4, 16% HP. Staraptor Def -1, SpD -1, Sharp Beak, Jolly, 115-167 Spe. Light Screen 3 turns. Foe back: Dragonite (Lum, Multiscale, Jolly, 93-145 Spe, Tailwind/ExtremeSpeed/Earthquake/Protect), Kingambit (LO, Supreme Overlord 3, Adamant, 55-102 Spe, KowtowCleave/IronHead/SuckerPunch/Protect). Staraptor has used Close Combat turns 6-7. Plan: Protect now. If Staraptor attacks, survive and Thunderbolt next. If Staraptor Tailwinds, expect Dragonite/Kingambit cleanup. Archaludon too weak to survive priority from either.

decisions.rationale: Arch at 16% with +4 Def still in range of Staraptor CC based on prior 22% at +3; CC is super-effective and best vs Steel types. Thunderbolt is weakened by -2 SpA and Light Screen, so Staraptor survives. Must KO Arch now as last mon vs 3.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO: Mega Zard Y Timid HW/WeatherBall/Hurricane/Protect, Whimsicott Bold Prankster Tailwind/Encore, Grimmsnarl Impish Light Clay screens, Archaludon Modest Stamina WiseGlasses TBolt/Flash/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand EQ/IceFang/TWave/Protect, Quaquaval Jolly MysticWater AquaStep/CC/IceSpinner/Protect. Leads Zard+Whim.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon at 16% HP cannot survive Close Combat from faster Staraptor. Protect ensures survival against the likely KO attempt, allowing Thunderbolt next turn. Thunderbolt risks losing Archaludon for uncertain gain, as Staraptor may prioritize the guaranteed KO.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Archaludon SpA -2, Def +4, 16% HP. Staraptor Def -1, SpD -1, Sharp Beak, Jolly, 115-167 Spe. Light Screen 2 turns. Foe back: Dragonite (Lum, Multiscale, Jolly, 93-145 Spe, Tailwind/ExtremeSpeed/Earthquake/Protect), Kingambit (LO, Supreme Overlord 3, Adamant, 55-102 Spe, KowtowCleave/IronHead/SuckerPunch/Protect). Staraptor has used Close Combat turns 6-7. Plan: Protect now. If Staraptor attacks, survive and Thunderbolt next. If Staraptor Tailwinds, expect Dragonite/Kingambit cleanup. Archaludon too weak to survive priority from either.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon at 16% +4 Def makes CC ~15-30% so no KO; its -2 SpA + Light Screen makes Thunderbolt ~26-42% vs our -1 SpD, so we survive. Protect stalls Light Screen final turn, wastes its low-odds Protect, and reveals opponent's second mon (Stunfisk/Quaquaval) before committing.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO: Mega Zard Y Timid HW/WeatherBall/Hurricane/Protect, Whimsicott Bold Prankster Tailwind/Encore, Grimmsnarl Impish Light Clay screens, Archaludon Modest Stamina WiseGlasses TBolt/Flash/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand EQ/IceFang/TWave/Protect, Quaquaval Jolly MysticWater AquaStep/CC/IceSpinner/Protect. Leads Zard+Whim. Archaludon gets +Def via Stamina, runs Draco for big drop.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Archaludon at 16% HP cannot survive Close Combat (min 23.9%). Staraptor has used Close Combat 3 times and is likely to use it again. Protect has 25% success but is the only way to survive this turn. Thunderbolt with SpA -2 may not KO (29.2-93.8%), and Archaludon faints before attacking if Staraptor uses Close Combat. Protect gives a chance to survive and attack next turn, even though game is likely lost to priority afterward.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Archaludon last mon, 16% HP, SpA -2, Def +4. Staraptor Def -1, SpD -1, Sharp Beak, Jolly, 115-167 Spe, has used Close Combat 3 times. Foe back: Dragonite (Lum, Multiscale, Jolly, 93-145 Spe, Tailwind/ExtremeSpeed/Earthquake/Protect), Kingambit (LO, Supreme Overlord 3, Adamant, 55-102 Spe, KowtowCleave/IronHead/SuckerPunch/Protect). Light Screen 1 turn left. Plan: Protect to survive Close Combat, then Thunderbolt next turn. Even if Staraptor is KO'd, Archaludon falls to priority from Dragonite/Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon 16% +4 Def: CC 43-92% at 0 boost => ~14-30% at +4, still best chance to KO vs BB 6-13%. Must remove Archaludon now before facing 1v3. Protect leaves it alive and wastes reduced Protect.

Staraptor outspeeds and guarantees a KO with Close Combat. Archaludon's Protect is the only way to block the immediate KO and potentially survive to attack next turn, aligning with the established plan.

Staraptor 167 > Archaludon 90-137 so CC goes first. Raw CC 43.7-92% max; /3 for +4 Def = ~14.6-30.7% so >16% current most rolls KO. Brave Bird is 0.5x vs Archaludon, worse. Protect gives free switch to full HP checks in 1v3. Best win chance is KO Archaludon now.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Staraptor outspeeds and has spammed Close Combat every turn; attacking risks immediate KO. Protect has reduced success (~33%) but is the only line that survives the turn. Even if Staraptor falls, priority from Dragonite/Kingambit likely ends the game, so maximizing survival this turn is the only meaningful play.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Archaludon last mon, 16% HP, SpA -2, Def +4. Staraptor Def -1, SpD -1, Sharp Beak, Jolly, 115-167 Spe, spams Close Combat. Foe back: Dragonite (Lum, Multiscale, Jolly, 93-145 Spe, Tailwind/ExtremeSpeed/Earthquake/Protect), Kingambit (LO, Supreme Overlord 3, Adamant, 55-102 Spe, KowtowCleave/IronHead/SuckerPunch/Protect). Light Screen 1 turn left. Plan: Protect to survive Close Combat, then Thunderbolt next turn. Even if Staraptor is KO'd, Archaludon falls to priority from Dragonite/Kingambit.

reflections.summary: Won because preview plan directly answered their sun HO core (Zard/Whim/Grim/Arch). Sneasler Rock Slide punished Mega Zard Y even on Protect turn, and Staraptor Intimidate + double Close Combat from Sneasler/Staraptor broke Stamina Archaludon despite Def boosts. Shadow Tag Gengar + Sinistcha absorbed early pressure while Fighting spam closed game.
reflections.adjustment: Don't feed Archaludon free Stamina with Rock Slide before committing Close Combats, and don't leave Sinistcha vs Draco. Next game expect Stunfisk-Galar and Quaquaval to check Fighting - keep Mega Gengar to trap Whimsicott/Grimmsnarl and preserve Staraptor Tailwind/Protect to play around Thunder Wave and Aqua Step boosts.
reflections.notebook: Opp sun HO: Mega Zard Y Timid HW/WeatherBall/Hurricane/Protect, Whimsicott Bold Prankster Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast/Protect Leftovers, Grimmsnarl Impish Light Clay screens FakeOut/PartingShot, Archaludon Modest Stamina WiseGlasses TBolt/Flash/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand EQ/IceFang/TWave/Protect, Quaquaval Jolly MysticWater AquaStep/CC/IceSpinner/Protect. Game1 bring: Zard/Whim/Grim/Arch, benched Stunfisk/Quaq. Tendencies: Zard Protects T1 vs Rock Slide, Archaludon spams Protect to stall Close Combat drops and fishes fails, targets Sinistcha with Draco. Leads Zard+Whim. Plan for next: keep Rock Slide + double Fighting core, keep Intimidate Staraptor for Archaludon, anticipate Stunfisk/Quaq adaptation.

reflections.summary: The team-preview plan was fundamentally flawed: bringing Charizard-Mega-Y (4x weak to Rock) and Archaludon (4x weak to Fighting) into an opponent leading with Sneasler and Staraptor guaranteed early losses to Rock Slide and double Close Combat. Archaludon was overwhelmed by Fighting spam and had no path to break through the intact Dragonite and Kingambit back end.
reflections.adjustment: Do not bring Charizard-Mega-Y or Archaludon against this team. Lead with a faster Fighting- and Rock-resistant Pokémon (e.g., a Ghost or Fairy type) to neutralize Staraptor and Sneasler, and bring a win condition that can outspeed or survive priority from Dragonite and Kingambit.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's core: Staraptor (Sharp Beak, Intimidate, spams Close Combat), Sneasler (Focus Sash, Rock Slide, Close Combat), Dragonite (Lum Berry, Multiscale, Tailwind/ExtremeSpeed/Earthquake), Kingambit (Life Orb, Supreme Overlord, KowtowCleave/SuckerPunch). Secondary: Sinistcha (Heatproof, Matcha Gotcha, Rage Powder), Gengar-Mega. Staraptor and Sneasler both carry Rock Slide and Close Combat, making Charizard-Mega-Y and Archaludon unplayable leads. Opponent relies on double Fighting spam and priority to close games.
